What else should I really know about string and character encoding in Java? Those bytes are interpreted differently depending on the character encoding they are assumed to be in. Thus, I'm refering to strings which contain `char`s that may be interpreted differently, either at runtime or at compile-time, by assuming the file was encoded in different character sets. * To be explicit about the compilation step, I used sun's encoding property to set the charset at compilation time: `javac -encoding windows-1252 Main.java`, with the encoding set appropriately. * Blog post I wrote on Java encoding. A summary of "what to know" about string encodings in Java:. String literals ends up in those class files with (sort of) UTF-8 encoding, regardless of the charset which the Java compiler used to interpret the source files. The locale on the system on which the Java compiler runs impacts how the source code is interpreted, but once the Java compiler has understood that your string contains the code point number 6, then this code point is what will make its way to the class files, and none other. Use of the default, locale-dependent encoding is fine when it is applied to some data exchanged with the user, such as a configuration file or a message to display immediately; but elsewhere, avoid locale-dependent methods whenever possible. Multiple Intrusion Detection System (IDS) sensors don't detect HTTP requests that use “%u” encoding. Reported September 05, 2001, byeEye Digital Security. ·         Cisco Secure Intrusion Detection System Sensor Component. ·         Internet Security Systems (ISS) RealSecure Network Sensor 5.x and 6.x prior to XPU 3.2. ·         Internet Security Systems (ISS) RealSecure Server Sensor 6.x prior to 6.0.1. ·         Internet Security Systems (ISS) RealSecure Server Sensor 5.5. ·         Enterasys Dragon IDS Sensor 4.x. ·         Snort, an open source Intrusion Detection System, prior to 1.8.1. MultipleIntrusion Detection System (IDS) sensors don't detect HTTP requests that use“%u” encoding. An attacker can use this vulnerability to evade IDSs whenmaking requests on a Web server that the IDS would typically detect, such asrequests for .ida files. eEye Digital Security's advisorydescribes a more detailed explanation of this vulnerability. The problem is that since %u encoding is not astandard IDS systems did not know about this IIS specific encoding and thereforeare not properly decoding %u requests and will not detect these attacks.”. ISS includes a patch in RealSecure Network Sensor X-Press Update 3.2. RealSecure Server Sensor 6.0.1 includes a fix for this vulnerability. Users can download RealSecure Server Sensor 6.0.1 from ISS's Web site. ISS X-Force recommends that all RealSecure customers upgrade their Windows Server Sensors to version 6.0.1. The vendor is developing a patch for RealSecure Server Sensor 5.5, which is available at the ISS Download Center http://www.iss.net/eval/eval.php. The Web processing engine of Dragon Sensor 5.0 already includes signatures to detect this encoding. ITPro Today's 2025 IT Priorities Report. results.content: # Head in the Clouds. HomeRe-Encoding MP3 files for faster playback speed. # Re-Encoding MP3 files for faster playback speed. While many music players can change the playback speed of files at runtime, a rather interesting exception is old-school mp3 players, and specifically water-proof mp3 players used by swimmers. And these tiny waterproof music players (I use the excellent Syryn player from Underwater Audio) just don’t have the oomph (or the interface) to change the playback speed of an audio stream at runtime. I will use the awesome ffmpeg open source library to re-encode my media files. To encode a single mp3 file run the following shell command:. $: ffmpeg -i some_file.mp3 -filter:a "atempo=2" some_file_x2.mp3.
